tagline: Up one long mountain and down through mustang country.
intro: From Frenchglen the loop climbs the west slope of Steens Mountain, a single fault-block mountain some fifty miles long. Sagebrush gives way to juniper, then to quaking aspen and mountain mahogany as the moisture rises, and the road goes on up to become the highest in Oregon. From the east rim the mountain drops more than a vertical mile to the floor of the Alvord Desert.
The end of the loop winds through the range of the South Steens wild horses, descended from mustangs that got away from explorers, settlers, miners and ranchers.
season: TripCheck gives July through October as the best time.

moments.title: Frenchglen
moments.text: The settlement is named for the French-Glenn Livestock Company, which built its headquarters here in 1872, and its old state-owned hotel stands at the north end of the loop road.

moments.title: Whorehouse Meadow
moments.text: Basque herders' carvings still mark the aspens around this meadow, which federal maps called Naughty Girl Meadow from the 1960s until public outcry brought the old name back in 1981.

moments.title: Kiger Gorge
moments.text: At the overlook you stand at the headwall of one of the mountain's five glacier-cut canyons, a U shape straight out of the textbook.

practical: TripCheck notes the road is closed in the winter months.
